content:
samir: Noticed a flaky failure in ruby-sampleapp CI after dependency bumps. Failing spec: `spec/auth_retry_spec.rb` — intermittent 401->retry hang. Happens ~25-35% of runs. Can't repro locally yet.

samir: CI log snippet:
```
E, [2026-03-22T18:14:02.890Z] ERROR -- : TokenRefreshError: 401 unauthorized
#<Thread:0x00007f9b8c0> run at auth_retry.rb:47
...
Timeout::Error: connection timed out waiting for reconnect
```

elaine: ack. Which packages bumped? Link the failing job and Gemfile diff?

samir: job: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ruby-sampleapp/actions/runs/1237890123 (private)
Gemfile.lock diff: Faraday 1.10 -> 2.0, net-http-persistent 3.x -> 4.0; also small tweak in our HTTP adapter wiring.

juan: sounds like a connection reuse change. Faraday 2 and net-http-persistent 4 changed pooling/eviction semantics. If the test stubs the token endpoint and then the client reuses a stale socket, retries could hang.

juan: question: does the spec stub at the HTTP layer or higher? If we're stubbing net/http responses but keeping the same connection, a 401->200 switch may not take effect until the socket resets.

samir: the spec uses WebMock but we have a helper that `allow_any_instance_of(HTTP).to receive(:request).and_call_original` in one case, so it's a bit leaky.

matt: short-term mitigation: mark the spec flaky and add an rspec retry metadata for CI. Longer term we should ensure the client resets connection after auth refresh.

elaine: propose implementing `reset_connection!` on our HTTP client wrapper, called after a successful token refresh following a 401. Example helper patch:
```ruby
# lib/redwood/http_client.rb
def reset_connection!
  if @conn && @conn.respond_to?(:finish)
    begin
      @conn.finish unless @conn.closed?
    rescue StandardError
      # best-effort cleanup
    ensure
      @conn = nil
    end
  end
end
```
This avoids touching adapter internals and works across net-http-persistent versions.

samir: I'll prepare a minimal PR: add `reset_connection!`, update the auth refresh path to call it, add a tiny spec asserting it's called, and mark the flaky test with a temporary `:flake` tag. Also expand the GH Actions matrix to include ruby 3.1 and 3.2 to catch regressions.

ci-bot: Rerun requested by @samir 1:33. :arrows_counterclockwise:

juan: review note: prefer checking `@conn&.closed?` before calling `finish` to avoid Errno::ENOTCONN on some net-http-persistent versions. Also add a comment referencing the Faraday/net-http-persistent changelog.

samir: updated patch per review, added the closed? guard and a comment. PR opened: #482 (https://github.com/redwood-inference/ruby-sampleapp/pull/482) with code, test, and CI tweak. PTAL.

elaine: quick thumbs on the PR from me. Please include Changlog entry and `chore(ruby): compat(net-http-persistent 4.x)` in the commit message so we can backport.

matt: can we add a cheap smoke test in our devex pipeline that exercises the auth-refresh path end-to-end? Would have caught this earlier. Keep it lightweight.

samir: added `smoke:auth-refresh` job that runs when files under `ruby/` change; it spins up a tiny rack app and runs one refresh scenario. Included in the PR.

ci-bot: CI rerun: green on second try.

elaine: moving to close after backport to `release/1.4.x`. cc @matt for release notes.

samir: release note draft: "ruby-sampleapp: make HTTP client resilient to connection reuse after auth refresh (compat with Faraday 2.x / net-http-persistent 4.x)."

matt: perfect. Thanks for the quick turnaround.
